correctness.rationale: Every complete nonalgebraic type is an ordered gap pair (i,j). Its exact disagreement number is \(i+j-2C_\pi(i,j)\), the symmetric difference cardinality of prefix sets. A one-disagreement type must lie in the \(2n\) off-diagonal neighboring cells; saturating all these cells forces \(\pi(k)\leq k+1\) and \(\pi^{-1}(k)\leq k+1\) for all k, equivalent to bandwidth one and precisely to a product of disjoint adjacent swaps. For each swap only C_pi(k,k) differs from identity, so \(P_\pi=P_{\mathrm{id}}+s(z^2-1)\). The c1 coefficient forces every preimage of that polynomial to be bandwidth one, and the constant coefficient forces its swap count s; nonadjacent swap starts are counted by \(\binom{n-s}{s}\). Independent direct comparison enumerated all 46,232 permutations of sizes 2..8 and matched the derived classifications and exact fibres. These finite tests are corroboration, not substitutes for the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The two primary sources establish the two-order Fraisse setting and (n+1)^2 gap-orbit grid but the inspected relevant text does not give the sharp one-disagreement extremal condition, the complete matching polynomial, or its exact fibres. Published mathematical-record searches using insertion/disagreement/bandwidth-one aliases returned related but noncovering results on unconditional inversions, Mallows-adjacent matchings and Simon-disagreement. A prior in-scope type-compatibility Smith form uses the same homogeneous model but proves an integral matrix invariant that neither states nor implies this weighted type-count classification. Priority remains provisional due to alternate terminology.

value.rationale: A one-point extension that reverses only one named comparison is a canonical near-agreement event in a homogeneous two-ranking structure. Its extremal count is a meaningful local type-statistic, and the theorem characterizes *all* extremizing finite bases at arbitrary size by bandwidth-one/matching structure. The full degree-spectrum fibre classification exposes an exact reconstruction obstruction: the spectrum knows how many independent swaps occur but not their locations, with binomially many distinct patterns. This is a complete motivated classification rather than an unmotivated small finite lookup.
